newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's return to erase China's disgrace - Qian.
newsitem.headline: HK's return to erase China's disgrace - Qian.

text.p: The disgrace and humiliation that China suffered for more than 150 years will disppear with the return of British-held Hong Kong to Chinese rule this year, Vice-Premier Qian Qichen said on Wednesday.

"Hong Kong will return to the embrace of the motherland (on July 1)," the Xinhua news agency quoted Qian as saying in a message to the people of Hong Kong to mark the Chinese Lunar New Year, their last under British rule.

"As a result, the disgrace and humiliation China has suffered from for more than 150 years will disappear," Qian said, referring to the unequal treaties China signed after its defeat by Britain in the mid-19th century and under which Hong Kong was handed over to Britain.
"This is a great event for the Chinese nation," Qian said in his new year greeting as Chinese worldwide usher in the Year of the Ox on Friday.
"The aspirations of several generations of Chinese people will come true," Qian said. Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
Qian reiterated China's promise not to poke its nose into Hong Kong's affairs.
"Hong Kong people governing Hong Kong and a high degree of autonomy stands rock-firm," he said.
However, just last week a China-appointed committee handling the handover of the British colony voted to roll back civil liberty laws in Hong Kong after July 1, triggering protests in the territory.

Hong Kong's first post-colonial chief executive-designate, shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa, defended China on Tuesday, saying the international community did not understand China's proposed changes in the territory's human rights laws.
Chinese officials repeated demands on Monday that confidential files on the colonial government's top officials be handed over to Beijing.
British officials have maintained that the issue was strictly between the present and future Hong Kong administrations.
Qian cited what he said was China's political stability, booming economy and rising international status as evidence that reunification with China would be good for Hong Kong.
"I believe that with the powerful backing by the motherland and common efforts of six million Hong Kong residents, Hong Kong will...continue to maintain its long-term prosperity and stability."
Just 146 days remain before the British colony Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule.
